identity_marker: bright orange Petzl Grigri belay device with a black plastic release handle and grooved metal internal cam
continuity_anchors: set against a brightly lit indoor climbing gym background with blurred colorful climbing holds on textured gray walls
video_goal: Demonstrate the correct visual sequence for threading a climbing rope into a Petzl Grigri and securing it to a harness with a locking carabiner.
single_prompt: A close-up shows hands holding a bright orange Petzl Grigri belay device with a black plastic release handle and grooved metal internal cam in the left hand and a thick dynamic climbing rope in the right hand. The camera shifts to an over-the-shoulder view as the left thumb pushes the black plastic release handle slightly to pivot and slide open the metal moving side plate. In a close-up, the right fingers pinch the climbing rope, folding it over to form a tight, U-shaped bight. From a first-person view, the bight of rope is pushed into the open Grigri, wrapping the curve of the rope around the internal grooved metal cam. An extreme close-up focuses on the engraved icons inside the Grigri, showing the top strand of rope aligning with the 'climber' icon and the bottom strand aligning with the 'hand' icon. Returning to a first-person view, the metal moving side plate is pivoted back into its original position, snapping shut over the seated rope. A close-up shows a right hand bringing a pear-shaped locking carabiner into the frame, positioning it next to the closed Grigri. From an over-the-shoulder view, the carabiner gate is pushed open with the thumb, and the nose of the carabiner is hooked through the two aligned metal attachment holes of the Grigri. In a first-person view, the carabiner, now holding the Grigri, is pushed downward to clip through the thick nylon belay loop of a worn climbing harness. A close-up captures fingers twisting the textured metal sleeve on the locking carabiner upward until it stops, visibly covering the nose of the gate. From an over-the-shoulder view, the left hand sharply pulls the top 'climber' side of the rope upward, while the right hand firmly grips the bottom 'brake' side of the rope downward. Finally, a close-up shows the internal cam of the Grigri visibly pivoting upward inside the device, pinching the rope tightly against the metal channel to arrest the upward pull, all set against a brightly lit indoor climbing gym background with blurred colorful climbing holds on textured gray walls.
